text:
alex: FYI a customer (Acme) opened a ticket — their requests are suddenly routing to eu-west even though they set region=us-west. High latency and auth failures. Suspect healthcheck state went stale after yesterday's probe rate-limit change.

maria: confirmed, I can reproduce with a pinned-bucket tenant. curl shows us-west header but route lands in eu-west.

ben: can you paste the curl and headers? also any correlation with heartbeat entries?

alex: here's short repro:

```bash
curl -v https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \n  -H "X-Region: us-west" \n  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

response trace shows `x-served-region: eu-west-1` and 2200ms p95.

sara: grabbing heartbeat logs for the edge probes for us-west. looks like last_probe for many edge nodes is `suppressed: true` starting 2165553000.

eng-platform-bot: probe-manager: suppression window applied to probe-group=us-west-edge due to rate-throttle. suppression_reason=probe_rate_limit, ttl=300s, applied_by=auto-scaler.

maria: aha — probe suppression removes those healthy endpoints from active pool, routing falls back to next available region (eu). That explains wrong-region routing + latency.

ben: does suppression also affect auth token refresh endpoints? customer saw intermittent 401s.

alex: yes, when requests hit eu-west they hit a different auth cache and token issuer, some tokens are scoped to us region, so we see 401s.

sara: quick mitigation idea: 1) reduce suppression TTL to 30s for us-west probe-group; 2) invalidate region health cache for this tenant; 3) create temporary routing pin to prefer us-west for pinned tenants. Thoughts?

ben: +1 to cache invalidation and TTL reduction. routing pin is heavier but OK as emergency. Who can flip TTL?

maria: I can flip the TTL via probe-config UI under `probe-groups/us-west-edge`. Setting `suppression_ttl_seconds` from 300 -> 30. Doing it now.

ops-bot: action: probe-config update requested by maria at 2165554400. change pending.

maria: done. invalidating region health cache for Acme now.

eng-platform-bot: health-cache: invalidated keys: tenant:acme:region-health at 2165554420. routing_agents notified.

alex: customer confirms improved latency, routing now to us-west, 120ms p95. Auth 401s stopped.

ben: root cause writeup draft: probe rate-limiter change earlier yesterday introduced more aggressive suppression for high-scan edge groups. suppression TTL was too long (5m) which allowed temporary suppression to induce cross-region failover for pinned tenants. Also exposed token scoping mismatch when routed to alternate region.

sara: follow-ups: (1) add canary policy to not suppress endpoints that serve pinned tenants; (2) add metric for "suppressed-endpoints impacting pinned-tenants"; (3) add short-circuit: if pinned header present, prefer local regardless of suppression for up to 1m.

alex: I've opened CR-4821 for the config change + tests. Assigning to eng-platform (ben) for the rules and to infra (sara) for metrics.

ben: noted. will add a regression test in e2e routing suite to ensure probe suppression doesn't cause cross-region routing for pinned tenants.

maria: closing loop with customer and sending summary. :thumbsup:

alex: thanks all. logging this under incident-js-216555 for postmortem.

sara: quick snippet of the heartbeat entry that showed suppression:

```json
{"probe_id":"usw-edge-12","timestamp":2165553200,"status":"suppressed","reason":"rate_throttle","suppression_ttl":300}
```

ben: that TTL is the magic number we changed. good catch.

alex: moving to resolved for now — will follow up in postmortem with timeline and mitigations.

maria: resolved for Acme. keeping the alert on for 2 more hours.

ops-bot: incident status: mitigated -> monitoring.

alex: thanks everyone.
